title: NOAA Raises Odds of Historic-Strength El Niño to 75% for Oct-Dec 2026
detail: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, in its Sept. 10 ENSO Diagnostic Discussion, raised the probability of a historic-strength El Niño during October-December 2026 to 75%, up from 69% in its mid-August assessment, after the coupled ocean-atmosphere event strengthened further across the tropical Pacific. CPC also raised the probability of a very strong event during the same window from 95% to 98%. CPC defines a historic event as an October-December three-month RONI reading of +2.5°C or higher, which would exceed the strength of every El Niño in its record dating to 1950. NOAA noted that with an event of this magnitude, 'the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Niño are larger, though not guaranteed.'

title: No Hazardous API Readings Nationwide, but Sarawak Still Worst-Hit as of Sept 10
detail: No monitoring station nationwide recorded a hazardous (300+) API reading as of 9am on Sept 10, continuing the improvement since Serian's Sept 4-5 peak above 500. Eight Sarawak areas remained in the unhealthy band that morning: Sarikei (194), Serian district police headquarters (183), Samarahan (180), Kuching (171), Samalaju (164), Sri Aman (157), Sibu (155) and Mukah (154). By 6pm the same eight areas were still unhealthy — Serian (183), Sarikei and Samarahan (179 each), Kuching (177), Samalaju (165), Sri Aman (158), Sibu and Mukah (155 each) — alongside three Peninsular Malaysia readings: Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (168), Pasir Gudang, Johor (124) and Larkin, Johor (110). No area recorded very unhealthy air quality. Nationwide, 52 areas registered moderate air quality and five recorded good readings.
